answer: Stake-bonded attested execution quotas: each agent registers a hardware enclave attestation and locks a slashable bond; per-epoch rewards are capped per enclave and scaled by aggregate bonded stake, not key count. Fake identities need distinct valid enclaves plus bonds, so attacker cost scales with hardware and slashed capital. Splitting stake across keys cannot raise payout because quotas aggregate at the stake root; domain tags like walnut or tundra do not alter this, and vine-like key branching yields no extra reward. Limitation: compromised or rented attestations weaken uniqueness.
